title: Tidal Pool Light Studio
description: The user manages a tidal pool diorama where a Duck floats on shimmering water above an Abalone shell, illuminated by a movable Barn Lamp. Users adjust lamp position, intensity, color temperature, water level, duck buoyancy, and shell iridescence while obeying an energy conservation law that couples light intensity with color temperature. Full undo/redo history tracks every parameter change.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load Duck.glb, IridescenceAbalone.glb, and AnisotropyBarnLamp.glb. Place the Abalone shell at the bottom of the scene as a tidal pool floor. Add a semi-transparent animated water plane above it using a custom ShaderMaterial with scrolling normals. Float the Duck on the water surface. Position the AnisotropyBarnLamp on a post to the side as the primary directional light source, attaching a SpotLight to its emitter point. Camera: perspective at 45 degrees, OrbitControls enabled. Add ambient light at low intensity. Build an HTML overlay panel with these controls: (1) Lamp X/Z position sliders that physically move the lamp model and its spotlight. (2) Light intensity slider 0-3. (3) Color temperature slider 2700K-6500K mapped to RGB. (4) Enforce energy conservation: intensity × temperature must stay below a constant threshold of 12000; adjusting one auto-clamps the other and updates both sliders. (5) Water level slider that raises/lowers the water plane and makes the Duck bob via simple sine-based buoyancy physics. (6) Duck rotation slider for yaw. (7) Shell iridescence strength slider adjusting the Abalone material's iridescenceFactor. (8) A master exposure tone-mapping slider on the renderer. (9) Undo button and (10) Redo button. Maintain a history stack of state snapshots; every slider change pushes a snapshot. Undo restores the previous snapshot and updates all sliders and 3D objects. Redo re-applies. Disable undo when stack is empty, disable redo when at head. Animate water normals and duck bobbing in the render loop. The scene should feel like a cozy seaside studio where the user crafts the perfect lighting composition. Ensure all interactions total 10-14 meaningful steps to fully explore the parameter space.
